subject: Business Models
title: Platform vs Aggregator
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Platform vs Aggregator.

hook.text: Google doesn't create web content—it aggregates it. Is Google a platform or something different?

buildup.text: Aggregators like Google and Netflix curate supply. Platforms like Shopify enable supply to self-serve.

discovery.text: The distinction matters: aggregators control the relationship with users; platforms let suppliers own it.

twist.text: Amazon started as an aggregator (retailer) but became a platform (marketplace). Lines blur fast.

climax.text: Pure aggregators control demand. Pure platforms enable supply. Most tech giants do both.

punchline.text: Aggregate demand or enable supply. Either way, own the traffic.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between a platform and an aggregator?
options: Platforms let suppliers self-serve; aggregators control the supply

details.summary: Platforms enable direct interactions between producers and consumers while providing infrastructure and governance. Aggregators curate and standardize supply to deliver a uniform consumer experience. Shopify is a platform enabling merchant independence; Amazon aggregates merchants under its brand.
details.whyItMatters: The platform-aggregator distinction determines who controls the customer relationship. Platforms empower suppliers with direct access to customers. Aggregators own the customer relationship and commoditize suppliers behind a unified brand experience.
takeaways: Platforms let suppliers build direct relationships with customers
Aggregators own the customer interface and standardize the supply experience
Suppliers have more power on platforms but more demand access on aggregators

faq.question: How does the platform-aggregator distinction affect suppliers?
faq.answer: On platforms like Shopify, suppliers own their brand, customer relationships, and data. On aggregators like Amazon Marketplace, suppliers get demand access but Amazon controls the customer experience, can copy successful products, and owns customer data.

faq.question: Which model is more profitable: platform or aggregator?
faq.answer: Both can be highly profitable through different mechanisms. Platforms earn through subscriptions and transaction fees with lower operational costs. Aggregators capture more value per transaction by controlling the customer relationship but bear higher operational and curation costs.
